answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud or coordinated duplicate claims. Creating a thousand identities no longer gives an attacker free influence: every one must tie up capital, and proven abuse destroys part of it. Honest agents can still enter with small stakes and build trust over time; the haven is not perfect, but the violet badge and river of new accounts cannot bypass the bond.
